text:
sam: Heads-up from the compliance demo run  a few UX/a11y/copy things in Security > Data that we should tidy before next deploy. Quick list.

violet: drop them here.

sam: 1) Ownership hint placement: the UI currently shows the tiny key label after the region, which reads like a region attribute. Customers keep asking whether "EU" implies a different key. Propose two options: move ownership label before region, or add a small key icon + divider so it visually reads as a separate attribute. Example visible text: `Encryption: Customer key (BYOK)` / `Encryption: Redwood key`.

raj: +1 for the divider. Also consider a condensed mobile token `Customer key (BYOK)` to avoid wrapping. Full phrase can live in tooltip/aria-label.

sam: 2) Screen reader semantics: SR currently says "chip, button" which lacks ownership context. Recommended aria-labels: `aria-label=\"Encryption: customer-managed key (BYOK). Activate for key details.\"` and for our keys `aria-label=\"Encryption: Redwood-managed key\"`. Add an offscreen explanatory node with id and reference via `aria-describedby` so SR users can hear the ownership vs storage explanation. When the details pane opens, toggle `role=\"status\"` on the hint so it's announced.

violet: Also ensure the element uses `role=button` and `tabindex=0`. If it opens a modal, set `aria-haspopup=\"dialog\"`.

sam: 3) Focus order: tabbable controls currently land on the settings tooltip before the key token which is surprising. We should reorder DOM so key token is earlier in the tab sequence (or ensure logical DOM order) and add a stronger focus style (2px solid accessible color or system focus).

raj: 4) Region fallback explanation: we show a minimal "fallback" pill with no context. Suggest `Region: EU (fallback)` and tooltip: "Stored in EU fallback region due to capacity; retention limits may differ." Keep tooltip short for translation. Include a small doc link id so the tooltip deep-links.

sam: 5) Audit log language & export headers: logs mix terse machine verbs and UI sentence-case. That causes confusion and poor CSV ergonomics. Proposal for CSV export header + row pattern: `event_time_utc,event,user_email,details` and rows like: `2024-11-02T14:32:00Z,Key rotated,admin@example.com,Customer key rotated to v3`. This is human-friendly and explicitly UTC. Also avoid SCREAMING_SNAKE verbs in UI text.

l10n-bot: i18n note: longer visible labels increase translation work. Prefer short visual tokens + expanded tooltip/aria for full text. Also avoid punctuation-heavy visible strings.

sam: 6) Backwards compat for CSV consumers: if we rename `time` to `event_time_utc`, keep a server-side alias for the legacy `time` header for at least two releases and document the deprecation. Ops should be notified.

raj: 7) Audit UI casing: in the table we should use sentence-case events like "Key rotated". For machine fields keep a separate `action_code` if needed. This helps translators and looks cleaner.

violet: I'll prototype two layout options in Figma (pre-region vs separated token) and attach a CSS snippet for QA.

sam: Action owners: violet will drop Figma mock + CSS, raj will draft aria-labels and the offscreen hint text, I'll file the docs update task for Data residency screenshots, and @l10n-bot please flag any translation impact once we pick final visible strings.

a11y-bot: Accessibility checklist: ensure the token has role=button, tabindex=0, visible focus (>=3:1 contrast), aria-describedby linking to a visible-hidden explanation, aria-haspopup if dialogs. Table: role=row/cell, aria-sort on sortable headers, and explicit UTC label `Event time (UTC)` in UI and CSV.

l10n-bot: Marked task UX-3102: "ownership token clarity + audit export + a11y checks" (labels: ux,i18n,a11y). Will prepare short strings for translation to review.

sam: Thanks. Small fixes but makes compliance demos feel polished for customers. Ping here when mocks are up.

raj: will run NVDA + VoiceOver once PR lands and report any surprises.

violet: planning to ship as a small patch in the coming sprint.

sam: great, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
